body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)=\{L_{pq}:L\in\mathcal F_G(\Sigma),\ e=(p,q)\}\), with \(\lambda_e\) identified if and only if \(|\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)|=1\)

sampling_model.design: Population covariance-specific identification in a recursive linear structural equation model; the main theorems contain no sampling randomness.
sampling_model.units: An \(n\)-vector of observed variables with covariance \(\Sigma\).
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is required; the query is the direct structural coefficient on \(e\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The disturbance covariance is not supplied and is recovered as \(\Omega(\Lambda)=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda)\); covariance-confidence-set inversion is outside the primary claim.

Theorem 14 places promise numerical edge identifiability in \(\forall\mathbb R\), and Corollary 5 gives a polynomial-space decision bound.

body.tldr: A covariance-specific coefficient can be generically recoverable yet ambiguous or singular at the covariance actually supplied. Maximum directed indegree one is the exact tractable side: a deterministic polynomial-bit algorithm normalizes every bi-affine fiber into pole-aware Möbius components and a singular-relation \(2\)-CNF, returning a unique rational coefficient, two unequal feasible witnesses, or a componentwise quadratic nonconstant-curve certificate. At indegree two, a private-parent and occurrence-hub compiler gives a bijection from an explicitly encoded planted-selector quadratic solution set onto the entire SEM fiber, yielding promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness. Relative to Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz, the hard-side delta is exactly maximum directed indegree two together with the fiber-bijective compiler.

project_justification.gap: Complete low-fan-in algorithms are generic and may divide by expressions that vanish at the observed covariance, whereas the published numerical-identification completeness construction permits unbounded directed fan-in and does not provide the bounded-fan-in fiber bijection required here.
project_justification.niche: The missing case is an all-covariance, polynomial-bit classification at fan-in one paired with a fiber-faithful lower bound at the next integer fan-in.
project_justification.fill: The Möbius-component and singular-clause normal form proves exact tractability with checkable low-degree certificates, while the private-slot compiler preserves the full source fiber at maximum directed indegree two. Rational strict diagonal dominance and the planted feasible matrix are construction normalizations, not separate novelty claims.

body.related_work: Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz define numerical edge identification at a feasible covariance and prove unrestricted promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness. The hard-side strict delta over their Corollary 4 is only maximum directed indegree two together with a compiler that is bijective on the complete real fiber; rational strict diagonal dominance and a supplied planted feasible matrix are retained as technical normalization properties rather than claimed advances. The fan-in-one theorem separately tightens their polynomial-space upper bound on that restricted class. Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz derive missing-cycle quadratic equations and document spurious-root behavior, which informs the componentwise quadratic representation. Gupta and Bläser prove complete randomized polynomial-time generic identification on directed trees using rank-two relation matrices, Möbius composition, and fractional affine square-root terms; that construction informs, but is not claimed to be subsumed by, the pointwise normalization. Briefs and Bläser accelerate the same generic tree target and are likewise treated as an algorithmic benchmark rather than a theorem target. Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant study graph-wide global identifiability, while Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give the half-trek sufficient criterion for generic rational identification; neither addresses a single exceptional covariance fiber. Ankan, Wortel, Bollen, and Textor connect latent-to-observed graphical identification to MIIV and identify the applied workflow that consumes the exact audit. Sankararaman, Louis, and Goyal study robust recovery under sufficient conditioning assumptions, and Mareis, Sturma, and Drton derive regular half-trek inference; conditioning and covariance-confidence-set inversion remain outside the primary theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The arbitrary-input normalization must be audited at every pole, zero polynomial, repeated quadratic root, and rank-one degeneration. The hard-side compiler must be checked after eliminating every copy equation, including repeated inputs, to rule out any extra coefficient branch. A single global primitive-element certificate is not required and can have exponential degree; all witnesses are therefore componentwise quadratic.
body.honest_scope: All formal statements are to be proved. Bounded symbolic checks in the presolve draft are evidence only. The central open proof obligations are the exact equivalence between the real fiber and the \(2\)-CNF normalization, the completeness of the exact planted-selector source language, and the fiber bijection for the complete selector-circuit compiler. The five-node multiplication instance verifies one full gate fiber but does not substitute for the composition proof. The proposal does not claim finite-sample inference, numerical stability near singular strata, or an exact latent-to-observed fiber bijection. As a sanity reduction, a two-node model with \(1\to2\) and no bidirected edge returns \(\lambda_{12}=\Sigma_{12}/\Sigma_{11}\), while adding the bow makes the attainable set all of \(\mathbb R\); on generic directed trees the finite component representation reduces to the one- or two-FASTP classification of Gupta and Bläser.
